answer: Correlated bonding lets an agent economy price sybil farms by cluster size. Each key holds a bond in a protocol vault, and once audits link keys to one operator, key number k in that cluster must keep 40×k² POA there or be frozen: two linked keys hold 200 in total, ten hold 15,400, and a 1,000-key farm about 13 billion, while a full epoch pays out near half a million. Bonds stay locked to a 30-epoch horizon, so a cluster caught copying late is still slashed whole. Weakness: links run like karst, hidden under separate hosts and wallets until timing or payment traces surface them.
